title: 5.3 Proving Triangle Congruence by SAS

icans: I can identify the included angle between two sides.
I can use SAS to decide whether two triangles are congruent.
I can write a proof that uses SAS.

vocab: the angle formed by two sides of a ___________
if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are congruent to two sides and the included angle of another, the ____________ are congruent

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Discovery: two sides and the angle between

blocks.p: Draw a 50° angle. Mark 4 cm on one ray and 6 cm on the other. Connect the endpoints.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Included angle: the angle _______________ two sides (formed by them).
SAS Congruence Theorem: if two sides and the _______________ angle of one triangle are congruent to two sides and the included angle of a second triangle, then the triangles are congruent.

blocks.stem: Can you prove the triangles congruent by SAS? If so, write the congruence statement.
A̅B̅ ≅ D̅E̅, B̅C̅ ≅ E̅F̅, and ∠A ≅ ∠D. Can you use SAS? Explain.

notes: Free parts: a shared side is congruent to itself by the _______________ Property, and vertical angles are congruent.

blocks.stem: A̅B̅ ≅ C̅B̅ and ∠ABD ≅ ∠CBD. Are △ABD and △CBD congruent? Explain.
Given: A̅B̅ ≅ C̅B̅ and B̅D̅ bisects ∠ABC.  Prove: △ABD ≅ △CBD.
Given: E is the midpoint of A̅C̅ and of B̅D̅.  Prove: △AEB ≅ △CED.
In △PQR and △XYZ: P̅Q̅ ≅ X̅Y̅, ∠Q ≅ ∠Y, and Q̅R̅ ≅ Y̅Z̅. Are the triangles congruent? Which theorem?
Given: M is the midpoint of A̅B̅ and of C̅D̅ (the segments cross at M).  Prove: △AMC ≅ △BMD.

tickets.stem: In △DEF, which angle is included between D̅E̅ and E̅F̅?
Two sides and a non-included angle are congruent. Can you use SAS?
Two triangles share a side. What is the reason the shared side is congruent to itself?
